## Design

### 2026-10-18 – GrabbiExtendo - Link done!

**5h**

GrabbiExtendo - Link done!

Used Fusion 360 and made a 88 mm bar with three 3.5mm pin holes(Small isn't it?) It turns out the hedge shears I have in my backyard which I showed in the video are way too heavy for the jaw and the overall structure to carry, so I decided to adapt my mechanism for regular pruning shears! Which are much smaller but still effective.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8gj7S6WIDaEIJSjTsLHoa4RS9wzwJHca/46f9017a1425c867a8a091eaef6cdc382eae9765c924ad586c6e1af66665709f.png)
Here is the frontal view, as you can see each bar forms an "X", and since there's 4 bars there's 2 "X" which are also connected. Now, to make two bars an "X" I used a revolute type joint in the hole of the middle, and then I duplicated it to make the second "X".
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8gj7S6WIDaEIJSjTsLHoa4RS9wzwJHca/edae5cbce629f3a3e453d76f8203d95d31db22ac770adb3a00f82d727f9a8aa9.png)
What really took me more time was trying to join these two, I dragged my cursor over an "X" and tried to drag it to fuse but it would just go over the second, or just stay behind it
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8gj7S6WIDaEIJSjTsLHoa4RS9wzwJHca/9095521d0b43809a552be4fa1aee99af17c78f79a7fa6b8c64e506eb5cc4c06b.png)
Point to point move type helped a lot! After that I only had to move to move it very little with free move and done.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8gj7S6WIDaEIJSjTsLHoa4RS9wzwJHca/009f43848247eb517e1d11bc32828aa9925788ec3b633db8ac90c9b0f8399990.png)
Also faced some problems when making the three circles, I was modifying the size of the circles but got a "over-constrained sketch" error, it turns out I had applied an "Equal" constraint to all three circles and modifying one that already had a set constraint was the issue, I had to delete them all and set the new final value first, then apply the constraints.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8gj7S6WIDaEIJSjTsLHoa4RS9wzwJHca/76f29186b53d948f7f9fa32d091da65969fc4e2dd283f0bde18f5e1e8b935839.png)
Also added the pins while writing this journal, I used an offset plane from the circles with 1mm of distance so I could replicate the head of a bolt(Which I also made if you see the pic). I'll add the rest of the pins once the whole thing is finished. I'll make the handle next.

### 2026-10-18 – GrabbiExtendo - Final design, and a well deserved rest

**10.7h**

GrabbiExtendo - Final design, and a well deserved rest

How did we get here? I spent all day  working on the GrabbiExtendo, and it's not like I'm lazy I just had very week with school and such. Anyways, I present thee, the GrabbiExtendo final design!
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8gj7S6WIDaEIJSjTsLHoa4RS9wzwJHca/23140b2ae6b8bf21d07615889da87bc7a7908f7218b5e96e0d6d9e7ddad5847f.png)
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8gj7S6WIDaEIJSjTsLHoa4RS9wzwJHca/cc44f26108c9adc3a6d4a0eaf9021465745affc9528e510257d87e5aa56a9dbf.png)

Let's divide the the GrabbiExtendo into parts cuz I'm not explaining everything with just two images
+ Gears(Joint finally more useful :O)
+ jaw
+ Links(Oh noo ,links)
+ Handles
+ How it work!

![Screenshot 2026-10-18 133551](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8gj7S6WIDaEIJSjTsLHoa4RS9wzwJHca/641046efb73d2d82d1463637343431a924ec2f42e243769019f3a8c2801e6ae0.png)
![Screenshot 2026-10-18 133615](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8gj7S6WIDaEIJSjTsLHoa4RS9wzwJHca/7ba13e39e86247799a195022de935d7b14117ca8fa68150674cf349c2972615b.png)
(Yes these two are both related)

  Remember the use of the word "Gear" in my previous reel? That was def a prediction, here we see two module-2 spur gears with 20 teeth, 40mm apart and the left one has a rotation of 9° for it to not collide when rotating with the revolute-type joint. Also, If you're wondering what those pieces in the first pic are(The ones that look like a throne), they are the couplers and idlers, the idler at the bottom spins a shaft that would be useful If I had made the cable trigger for it to connect with a lever in the handles and make the entire thing spin with it, of course that's going to change in the building week!

![Screenshot 2026-10-18 152725](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8gj7S6WIDaEIJSjTsLHoa4RS9wzwJHca/9bcac93bf3cd1843ec33a4bc3326f12b91fa68dce8c03e6d90428d9247891744.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8gj7S6WIDaEIJSjTsLHoa4RS9wzwJHca/90288cccfe07f5f96d93a82f2c5658d189b97210e002a0c733f623672a45f1ae.png)
(Behold! The jaw and base!)

Two fingers, and each is a four-bar parallelogram driven by a crank on the gear, and since the gear is connected the pad faces will always stay parallel. There's also TPU strip lines for a stronger, safer grip and the gears can only rotate so the grooves stop at 25mm apart, which is the width of regular pruning shears(smaller ones, not the massive ones in my first reel)

![Screenshot 2026-10-18 191612](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8gj7S6WIDaEIJSjTsLHoa4RS9wzwJHca/80860a5c9427f60c591d123417e037e0623876e8e73b03ad78f1b034573d87ae.png)

Now, let's start connecting em shall we? As you can see here I tried making a plate to connect the jaw to the chain. There's a slot for a sliding pin, tho I couldn't get the sliding thingy to work, there's a few types of joints I still don't know how to use, might look up about them later.

![Screenshot 2026-10-18 195848](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8gj7S6WIDaEIJSjTsLHoa4RS9wzwJHca/9bd458ad4d116a6d65ae268aee77f0a2ab93d8eade7df32db659dce2767dca96.png)
(Connected! Using a revolute-type joint)

![Screenshot 2026-10-18 213410](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8gj7S6WIDaEIJSjTsLHoa4RS9wzwJHca/f7335c11ac2f4ca8554554b7860c800545fbbe3d70c56ded16b79c491b79ba0c.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-18 221133](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8gj7S6WIDaEIJSjTsLHoa4RS9wzwJHca/772d9d5be626281cee5b57fc2ae8ef413e45f0c282cf08716bdc6551e4bd9899.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8gj7S6WIDaEIJSjTsLHoa4RS9wzwJHca/64bcb5234611dee366e3c94b8e99e69e426c5b058aee2caea4821eecab9804d3.png)

Both handles are here! They're large and squeezing them stretches the chain, I also added the trigger lever on a pin to pull the jaw, I had also made a cable hole but I didn't have enough time this ocurrence.

So yeah, that's the progress of today, grand changes are the jaw-type and the pruning method, I had to leave out trying to make my GrabbiExtendo be able to grip the massive Hedge pruning shears since they were 1.7Kg and I'd have to make a much more advanced contraption

Still, I'm planning on finishing the cable routing, sliding pin and fixing the joints in the future, to guarantee printing doesn't come with any issues.
